content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Is it possible to connect two [product_name] PLCs located on separate subnets? PLC1: 192.168.1.2 PLC2: 192.168.0.3 Thank you.

You're referring to different IP address ranges, not actual subnets. The router, the [product_name] devices, and the PC (which runs the relevant software) all need to be configured within the same IP range. The first three parts of the IP address should match. Example: WWW.XXX.YYY.ZZZ WWW.XXX.YYY must be identical, and ZZZ should be unique for each device. The subnet mask, such as 255.255.255.0, should also be the same for all devices.

Yes, it's possible, but you'll need an IP gateway to enable communication between different subnets. In your network setup, you should configure the IP address, subnet mask, and gateway. This gateway allows devices across separate subnets to connect. If you're unsure, it's best to consult an IT specialist.
I am not entirely certain, but you might be able to connect the devices if you set the subnet mask to 255.255.0.0. In that case, both 192.168.1.2 and 192.168.0.3 could communicate.
